rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night is the day’s opposite: a realm of stillness, contraction, concealment, and latent things.
rows.anchor: الليل } أي الذي هو ضد النهار فهو محل السكون والانقباض والكمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night progressively covers the sun at sunset, extending the earth’s shadows and darkening the eastern horizon for longer or shorter periods.
rows.anchor: أي يغطي الشمس فيذهب ضوءها حين تغيب فتمتد ظلال الأرض على وجهها المماس لنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night’s fading light figures bodily nature veiling intellect through its corrupt temperament and poor constitution.
rows.anchor: كما يغطي البدن نور العقل بواسطة طبعه بخبثه ورداءة عنصره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night’s gradual covering contrasts with day, which reveals the sun at once when clouds and haze are absent.
rows.anchor: لأن الليل لا يذهب الضياء بمرة بل شيئا فشيئان ولا ينفك عن نور بخلاف النهار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is the encompassing field and display for the celestial processes just described.
rows.anchor: أي التي هي محل ذلك كله ومجلاه كما أن الأبدان محل النفوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky’s ordered construction points toward realities beyond what description can encompass.
rows.anchor: أي هذا البناء المحكم الذي ركب فيه ما ذكره إشارة إلى ما وراءه مما يعجز الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is humanity’s bedding and the setting for rational action; God spread it around living creatures beneath the celestial spheres.
rows.anchor: أي التي هي فراشكم بمنزلة محال تصرفاتكم بالعقل في المعاني المقصودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth’s floating, surrounding, and dangerous qualities also symbolize aspects of human striving.
rows.anchor: أي بسطها على وجه هي فيه محيطة بالحيوان كله ومحاط بها في مقعر الأفلاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The outward cosmos has an inward human counterpart, so celestial and terrestrial features can be read as faculties and bodily processes.
rows.anchor: وليس في العالم الآفاقي شيء إلا وفي العالم النفساني نظيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven heavens correspond to layers of the head and its cognitive and sensory faculties; the sun is spirit, night temperament, day heart, and moon soul.
rows.anchor: فالسماوات سبع كطباق الرأس التي تتعلق بالقوى المعنوية والحسية كالذاكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inner organs resemble stars; rain, heat, cold, thunder, lightning, and winds correspond respectively to tears, grief, joy, speech, salt, and breath.
rows.anchor: والأمطار كالدمع , والحر كالحزن , والبرد كالسرور , والرعد كالنطق , والبرق كالملح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lower world’s seven layers correspond to body layers; mountains resemble bones, and minerals and waters resemble bodily fluids and excretions.
rows.anchor: والعالم السفلي سبع طباق أيضا , قال الملوي : ( ونظيرها طبقة الجلد )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Vegetation resembles hair, while animals and birds resemble lice and fleas; the body’s front is inhabited and its back ruined.
rows.anchor: والنبات كالشعور تارة تحلق كالحصاد وتارة تقلع كالنتف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soul is the cosmos’s most wondrous and comprehensive feature, balanced from discordant mixtures into a harmonized whole.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت النفوس أعجب ما في الكون وأجمع , عبر فيها بالتسوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath’s implied conclusion is that God gave souls differing dispositions and capacity for purification or corruption, urging people to purify themselves in view of resurrection.
rows.anchor: جواب القسم مقدر تقديره : لقد طبع سبحانه وتعالى نفوسكم على طبائع متباينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah demonstrates God’s complete, freely chosen governance of souls through people’s divergent efforts despite sharing aims.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على مقصود الشمس ، وهو التصرف التام في النفوس بإثبات كمال القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its name, al-Layl, signals that night frustrates ordinary desire through darkness and sleep, the sibling of death.
rows.anchor: ليل نفسه دال على ذلك لأنه على غير مراد النفس بما فيه من الظلام والنوم الذي هو أخو الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the preceding surah’s account of purified and corrupted souls and Thamud’s fate, people diverge between good and evil while God governs souls through piety and wickedness.
rows.anchor: لما بين في الشمس حال من زكى نفسه وحال من دساها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night signifies confusion and obscurity, gradually covering what daylight made visible; it is suited to secrecy.
rows.anchor: أي يغطي ما كان من الوجود مبصرا بضياء النهار على التدريج قليلا قليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Day signifies disclosure: sunlight exposes what was hidden and removes all obscurity, suiting public action.
rows.anchor: أي ظهر ظهورا عظيما بضياء الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those seeking secrecy choose night and those seeking publicity choose day, whether righteous or wicked.
rows.anchor: فمن كان يريد السر قصد الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Male and female differ physically and figuratively: the male signifies aspiration and strength, the female lower aspiration and weakness.
rows.anchor: الذكر } أي حسا بآلة الرجل ومعنى بالهمة والقوة { والأنثى } حسا بآلة المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Using ما, often associated with nonrational things, recalls that idolaters treated God as though He were like their mindless idols.
rows.anchor: وحكم التعبير بما الأغلب فيه غير العقلاء ما تقدم في سورة الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording uses reciprocal omission: naming creation first implies its creator, while naming the creator second implies the omitted creation.
rows.anchor: فالآية من الاحتباك : ذكر أولا الصنعة دلالة على حذفها ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though people pursue a common end, their beliefs and actions radically diverge; one seeks deliverance and another ruins himself, so their outcomes cannot all be alike.
rows.anchor: إن سعيكم } أي عملكم أيها المكلفون في التوصل إلى مقصد واحد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr links the oath to the preordained divergence of creatures, by which God tests who does best.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام أبو جعفر بن الزبير : لما بين قبل حالهم في الافتراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The divergent efforts connect to the one who purifies or corrupts the soul; the following promise and threat explain that good and evil occur by God’s inspiration and decree.
rows.anchor: قد أفلح من زكاها وقد خاب من دساها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God inspires giving, piety, charity, miserliness, self-sufficiency, and denial; He created people and their deeds, acts without being questioned, and owns guidance and both worlds, against Qadariyya and Muʿtazila.
rows.anchor: فهو سبحانه الملهم للإعطاء والاتقاء والتصدق , والمقدر للبخل والاستغناء والتكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver gives what God prescribed and commanded, while the God-fearing person protects himself through obedience and avoiding sins.
rows.anchor: { فأما من أعطى } أي وقع منه إعطاء على ما حددنا له وأمرناه به { واتقى * }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥusnā is the excellent word of justice: monotheism and its related promises about the afterlife, worldly provision, and Islam’s triumph.
rows.anchor: وهي كلمة العدل التي هي أحسن الكلام من التوحيد وما يتفرع عنه من الوعود الصادقة بالآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares the truthful giver for the easy path through mercy, enabling pleasing conduct, a good life, and entry into Paradise; obedience itself can feel burdensome to the self.
rows.anchor: فقال : { فسنيسره } أي نهيئه بما لنا من العظمة بوعد لا خلف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser withholds what was commanded or encouraged; istaghnā means seeking independence from people and from promised reward through vain assumptions.
rows.anchor: واستغنى } أي طلب الغنى عن الناس وعما وعد به من الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser denies al-ḥusnā, rejecting that it deserves to be believed.
rows.anchor: أي أوقع التكذيب أن يستحق التصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prepares the denier for the hardest, most wretched path: deeds that incur divine anger and lead to Hell.
rows.anchor: للعسرى * } أي للخصلة التي هي أعسر الأشياء وأنكدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majestic plural signals how unlikely either path is: good is hard because surrounded by aversions, while reason and primordial nature warn against evil.
rows.anchor: وأشار بنون العظمة في كل من نجد الخير ونجد الشر إلى أن ارتكاب الإنسان لكل منهما في غاية البعد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s maxim says each person is made easy for the path for which he was created, supporting the prior decree of each outcome.
rows.anchor: وكما قال صلى الله عليه وسلم - ميسر لما خلق له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The miser’s wealth cannot save him when he falls into the grave or Hell; the verb can signify ruin or falling into a pit.
rows.anchor: أي هلك بالسقوط في حفرة القبر والنار , تفعل من الردى وهو الهلاك والسقوط في بئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening may be read as a rhetorical question, which denies the wealth’s benefit emphatically.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون استفهاما إنكاريا فيكون نافيا للإغناء على أبلغ وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has graciously committed Himself to show the true path and establish clear proofs; no one has an entitlement over Him.
rows.anchor: للهدى * } أي البيان للطريق الحق وإقامة الأدلة الواضحة على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both the present and the afterlife belong to God, who alone controls giving and withholding; rejecting His guidance harms only the rejecter.
rows.anchor: فمن ترك ما بينا له من طريق الهداية لم يخرج عن كونه لنا ولم يضر إلا نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is named before this world for the deniers’ concern, not merely for cadence; the author rejects treating Qur’anic ordering as rhyme or poetic meter.
rows.anchor: فقد ثبت بطلان هذا وأنه لا يحل اعتقاده في غير موضع , منها آخر سورة براءة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fire blazes intensely without effort from its keepers; the omitted tāʾ and assimilation suggest even the least fire of the afterlife is severe.
rows.anchor: وفي الإدغام أيضا إشارة إلى أن أدنى نار الآخرة كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the most wretched, meaning the unbeliever, undergoes the fire permanently; a sinful believer may enter but will not remain there.
rows.anchor: فإن الفاسق وإن دخلها لا يكون ذلك له على طريق اللزوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who lied and turned away corrupted his knowing faculty by arrogantly rejecting truth and refusing to give wealth for self-purification.
rows.anchor: الذي كذب } أي أفسد قوته العلمية بأن أعرض عن الحق تكبرا وعنادا فلم يؤت ماله لزكاة نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most God-fearing has reached the peak of piety by avoiding both idolatry and sins; a lesser sinner may enter the fire and later leave.
rows.anchor: الأتقى * } أي الذي أسس قوته العلمية أمكن تأسيس , فكان في الذروة من رتبة التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Giving wealth means spending it on good causes, thereby purifying and cultivating the self and replacing bad character with good.
rows.anchor: الذي يؤتي ماله } أي يصرفه في مصارف الخير , ولذلك بينه بقوله تعالى : { يتزكى * } أي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses reciprocal omission: mentioning denial first implies its opposite later, while mentioning giving later implies its opposite was omitted first.
rows.anchor: والآية من الاحتباك : ذكر التكذيب أولا دليلا على حذف ضده ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The giver seeks no repayment for anyone’s favor; the detached exception marks his sole aim as seeking his Lord’s pleasure.
rows.anchor: من نعمة تجزى * } أي هي مما يحق جزاؤه لأجلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s “face” signifies His essence and the highest aim: the giver seeks neither worldly gain nor even an afterlife reward.
rows.anchor: فلا نظر له إلا إلى ذاته سبحانه وتعالى التي عبر عنها بالوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises that the giver will be satisfied with the highest Paradise and further reward, with a promise that cannot fail.
rows.anchor: ولسوف يرضى * } أي بإعطاء الجنة العليا والمزيد بوعد لا خلف فيه

rows.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
rows.claim: Al-Zubayr ibn Bakkār reports that Abū Bakr freed vulnerable Muslims; when his father suggested buying someone to protect him, Abū Bakr said that was precisely his aim.
rows.anchor: نقل البغوي رضي الله تعالى عنه عن الزبير يعني ابن بكاري

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: The report attributes to Abū Bakr the reply that he wanted the freed people to protect him, not to purchase a worldly defender.
rows.anchor: كان أبو بكر رضي الله عنه يبتاع الضعفاء فيعتقهم فقال له أبوه : أي بني ! لو كنت تبتاع من يمنع ظهرك

rows.speaker: زهرة
rows.claim: When Quraysh blamed the idols for a freed woman’s blindness, Zahra rejected their power and her sight returned.
rows.anchor: وأم عميس وزهرة فأصيب بصرها حين أعتقها , فقالت قريش : ما أهذب بصرها إلا اللات والعزى , فقالت : كذبوا

rows.speaker: الزبير بن بكار
rows.claim: The report lists Abū Bakr’s freeing of al-Nahdiyya, her daughter, and a girl of Banū al-Muʾammal.
rows.anchor: وأعتق النهدية وابنتها وجارية بني المؤمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abū Bakr bought Bilāl from Umayya ibn Khalaf while Bilāl was tortured at midday, repeatedly crying “One, One”; the idolaters alleged a prior favor, which revelation refuted.
rows.anchor: وقال : إنه اشترى بلالا من أمية بن خلف استنقاذا له مما كان فيه من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that Abū Bakr would be pleased connects to the promise that God’s gift will satisfy the Prophet; Abū Bakr is the closest of the community to the Prophet’s station.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه أقرب أمته إلى مقامه لأنه مما وعد النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يرضيه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet’s statement that God and the believers would accept only Abū Bakr supports his unique closeness and the contrast between his striving and the worst unbeliever’s.
rows.anchor: يأبى الله والمؤمنون إلا أبا بكر رضي الله عنه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpreters say spiritual light from night prayer and other good deeds will bring sensory light after death.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم : إن المراد بالتجلي بالنور المعنوي من إنارة ظلام الليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s purpose is to show that the most God-fearing person remains in divine favor in both lives through perfected qualities that lead to the goal.
rows.anchor: مقصودها الدلالة على آخر الليل بأن أتقى الأتقياء الذي هو الأتقى على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title al-Ḍuḥā captures this purpose because its physical daylight symbolizes the spiritual light of perfected character.
rows.anchor: التي هي الإيصال للمقصود بما لها من النور المعنوي كالضحى بما له من النور الحسي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by midmorning, the daylight’s finest and brightest portion, suits the most honored creature and signals his exceptional rank.
rows.anchor: فذكر ماهو أشرف النهار وألطفه وهو زهرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sajā can mean that night’s people become still or that its darkness, covering, and blackness settle evenly; al-mustajī means covered.
rows.anchor: إذا سجى * } أي سكن أهله أو ركد ظلامه وإلباسه وسواده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternation of mixed and pure light and darkness can represent Qur’anic clear and ambiguous teachings and human spiritual conditions.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون الأول مشيرا إلى ما يأتي به هذا الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم من المحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart’s light can overcome the soul’s darkness, while appetite can darken the whole person; spirit or temperament then elevates or degrades the person.
rows.anchor: فروحه نور بنور القلب , فإن قويت شهوة النفس على نورانية القلب أظلم جميعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When spirit dominates temperament, a person rises beyond the rank of angels; when temperament dominates, a person falls below beasts.
rows.anchor: وإن غلب الروح على الطبع تروحن فارتفع عن رتبة الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When temperament dominates, a person falls below the rank of beasts.
rows.anchor: وإن غلب الطبع على الروح أنزله عن رتبة البهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God did not leave the Prophet in a separation like that of a departing person; God is his Lord who created, perfected, and nurtured him.
rows.anchor: ما ودعك } أي تركك تركا يحصل به فرقة كفرقة المودع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb qalaa denies hatred as well as abandonment; omitting its object shortens the wording while widening the meaning.
rows.anchor: وما قلى * } أي وما أبغضك بغضا ما , وحذف الضمير اختصارا لفظيا ليعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verses were revealed after revelation paused: the Prophet had promised answers about the Spirit, the Cave Companions, and Dhū al-Qarnayn without saying “if God wills,” prompting claims that his Lord had forsaken him.
rows.anchor: سألوه عن الروح وقصة أهل الكهف وذي القرنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the verses came, the Prophet said takbīr; the author says takbīr became a practice in this surah and those that follow.
rows.anchor: ولما نزلت كبر صلى الله عليه وسلم فكان التكبير فيها وفيما بعدها سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage distinguishes four relations: obedient believers are near and loved, unbelievers distant and hated, sinful believers mixed, and unbelievers’ outward worship has no acceptance.
rows.anchor: وقد أفهمت هذه العبارة أن المراتب التقريبية أربع

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr says the predestination discussion could cause fear, so God reassured His dearest servant by recounting his favor and the good of both lives.
rows.anchor: أنس تعالى أحب عباده إليه وأعظمهم منزلة لديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessings recall the Prophet’s mercy and gentleness toward believers, as described in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: عزيز عليه ما عنتم حريص عليكم بالمؤمنين رؤوف رحيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening’s hidden night recalls uncertainty about one’s path and destiny; remembering the signs and seeking refuge in God bring certainty.
rows.anchor: برفع القسم في الأولى بقوله :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some servants gain clear insight through steadfast piety and reflection, moving from inference to direct recognition of the path.
rows.anchor: بل قد يطلع سبحانه خواص عباده - بملازمته التقوى والاعتبار - على واضحة السبيل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet told Ḥāritha, and similarly Abū Bakr, that he had found the truth and should remain firm in it.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم لحارثة : ( وجدت فالزم ) وقال مثله للصديق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful receive good news in both lives and angelic reassurance, walking by a light God grants them.
rows.anchor: لهم البشرى في الحياة الدنيا وفي الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s consolation is linked to promises of angels’ protection and God-given light and discernment.
rows.anchor: يجعل لكم نورا تمشون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author compares guided believers to someone brought from death into light, unlike one trapped in darkness.
rows.anchor: أو من كان ميتا فأحييناه وجعلنا له نورا يمشي به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful gain clear insight through piety, detach from worldly hopes, and prepare for the afterlife through excellent deeds.
rows.anchor: فقطعوا عن الدنيا الآمال , وتأهبوا لآخرتهم بأوضح الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening night evokes the beginning’s obscurity, while the manifest day evokes the clarity reached by people whose hearts God has strengthened.
rows.anchor: فلابتداء الأمر وشدة الإبهام والإظلام أشار قوله سبحانه وتعالى : { والليل إذا يغشى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The many human paths reduce to belief or disbelief and to Paradise or Hell, as paired creation and flight toward God indicate.
rows.anchor: ولانحصار السبل وإن تشعبت في طريقي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah unfolds the blessings summarized at the end of al-Ḍuḥā and defines gratitude as strenuous worship and turning to God in hope.
rows.anchor: مقصودها تفصيل ما في آخر الضحى من النعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The title al-Sharḥ points to the surah’s purpose of explaining divine generosity and mercy.
rows.anchor: وعلى ذلك دل اسمها الشرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening interrogative is a forceful reminder that the chest-expansion is established, not a real question; mentioning favor before forgiveness foregrounds honor.
rows.anchor: فقال مثبتا لها في استفهام إنكاري مبالغة في إثباتها عند من ينكرها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās is cited for the view that al-Sharḥ is a Medinan surah.
rows.anchor: فإن هذه السورة مدنية عند ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expanded the Prophet’s chest through the Hijra, honoring and strengthening him, opening and washing his heart, and filling it with faith, wisdom, compassion, knowledge, and mercy.
rows.anchor: ونملأه إيمانا وحكمة ورأفة وعلما ورحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening was both a real event repeated several times and a metaphor for the meanings realized in the Prophet; knowledge concerns God and both lives, while wisdom puts things in their proper place.
rows.anchor: وقد كان هذا الشرع حقيقة مرارا , وكان مجازا أيضا بإحلال جميع معانيه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر المنصور
rows.claim: The source reports a reading attributed to Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr that opens the final consonant of nashraḥ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر المنصور بفتح جاء ( نشرح )

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya explains that reading as emphasis with a light nūn, replaced by an alif and then deleted for ease.
rows.anchor: وخرجها ابن عطية على التأكيد بالنون الخفيفة ثم أبدل ألف من النون

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān cites al-Liḥyānī’s report that some Arabs use the subjunctive after lam and the jussive after lan.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حيان بأن اللحياني حكى في نوادره عن بعض العرب النصب بلم والجزم بلن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The majority’s jussive reading suggests that the opening both expands the heart and firmly contains the knowledge and piety placed within it.
rows.anchor: ووجه قراءة الجمهور أنه لما دل على الفتح بالشرح دل بالجزم على أنه مع ذلك رابط

rows.speaker: ابن برجان
rows.claim: Ibn Barjān distinguishes the inward state of prophet and saint from the unbeliever, whose darkness prevents accepting guidance and rising through reflection.
rows.anchor: قال ابن برجان : ففرق ما بين النبي والولي في باطنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God raised the Prophet’s remembrance through his virtues, prophethood, migration, and the pairing of his name with God’s in testimony, call to prayer, prayer, and sermons.
rows.anchor: في كلمة التوحيد والإيمان والإذان والإقامة والتشهد والخطبة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī’s account continues by saying that the Prophet’s community received an abundant share of this honor.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : ثم جعل لأمته من ذلك أوفر الحظ

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Asked who God’s friends are, the Prophet answered that they are those whose mention brings God to mind.
rows.anchor: قيل : يا رسول الله , من أولياء الله ؟ قال : ( الذين إذا ذكروا ذكر الله )

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A related report describes God’s friends as people whose sight reminds others of God.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث : ( الذين إذا رؤوا ذكر الله )

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The best people are those whose appearance recalls God, speech increases knowledge, and actions inspire detachment from worldly life.
rows.anchor: وقال : ( خياركم من تذكر الله رؤيته , ويزيد في علمكم منطقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The highest praise is to have the Prophet’s remembrance joined with God’s remembrance.
rows.anchor: فمنتهى قسمة الثناء أن خلط ذكره بذكره

rows.speaker: خديجة
rows.claim: Khadīja described the Prophet as bearing others’ burdens, feeding guests, maintaining kinship, and helping those struck by hardship.
rows.anchor: قالت الصديقة الكبرى خديجة رضي الله تعالى عنها - ( الكل , ويقري الضيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Prophet endured extraordinary abuse, God promised to ease his burden, soften hearts, establish Islam, enrich and strengthen his companions, and open lands to them.
rows.anchor: بشره الله تعالى بأنه ييسر له جميع ذلك ويلين قلوبهم فيظهر دينه على الدين كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reversal from hardship to ease proves that God acts freely, changing conditions by choice rather than by necessity.
rows.anchor: فإنه قضى سبحانه وتعالى قضاء لا يرتد أنه يخالف بين الأحوال , دليلا قاطعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second statement answers those asking what follows hardship; its repeated definite al-ʿusr denotes the same hardship, while the indefinite ease is another ease.
rows.anchor: إن مع العسر } أي المذكور فإنه معرفة , والمعرفة إذا أعيدت معرفة كانت غير الأولى

rows.speaker: الحسن البصري
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reports that, when the verse was revealed, the Prophet said that one hardship would not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: فقال الحسن البصري : إن الآية لما نزلت قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( أتاكم اليسر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says that if hardship were in a lizard’s hole, ease would follow it until bringing it out.
rows.anchor: وروى عبد الرزاق عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه قال : ( لو كان العسر في جحر ضب

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: A Prophetic version from Ibn Masʿūd says ease would enter even a lizard’s hole; al-Haythamī grades its chain weak because it contains Abū Mālik al-Nakhaʿī.
rows.anchor: وللطبراني عنه رضي الله عنه قال : قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( لو كان العسر في جحر

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarānī and al-Bazzār report a similar saying from Anas; al-Haythamī calls its chain weak because it contains ʿĀʾidh ibn Shurayḥ.
rows.anchor: ورواه الطبراني أيضا في الأوسط والبزار عن أنس رضي الله عنه بنحوه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet came out smiling and repeated that one hardship would not defeat two eases.
rows.anchor: وروى الفراء عن الكلبي عن أبي صالح عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خرج

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar sent Abū ʿUbayda in Syria the saying that one hardship would not defeat two eases; Ibn Ḥajar considers this report’s route the strongest.
rows.anchor: وفي الباب عن عمر ذكره مالك في الموطإ عن زيد بن أسلم عن أبيه عن عمر

rows.speaker: سعد الدين التفتازاني
rows.claim: Al-Taftāzānī lays out four cases for repeating a noun as definite or indefinite, with a repeated indefinite ordinarily indicating a different referent and a definite the same one.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ سعد الدين التفتازاني في أول تلويحه في الكلام على المعرفة والنكرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects the grammatical rule as absolute: definiteness need not mean totality, context can defeat identity, and a repeated definite can refer to something different.
rows.anchor: وفيه نظر , أما أولا فلأن التعريف لا يلزم أن تكون للاستغراق بل العهد هو الأصل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The usual rule is only a default without contextual clues: repeating a definite normally preserves its referent, while a repeated indefinite normally changes it.
rows.anchor: قال : واعلم أن المراد أن هذا هو الأصل عند الإطلاق وخلو المقام عن القرائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeated definite nouns can change referent; the examples include scripture, enmity, ranks, and a requested book, while a poet’s repeated “time” would be pointless if identical.
rows.anchor: وقال تعالى : ( اهبطا بعضكم لبعض عدو ) [ البقرة : 36 ] وقال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An indefinite noun can repeat with the same referent, as in God being deity in heaven and earth, a requested sign, and human weakness followed by strength and weakness.
rows.anchor: وإلا فقد تعاد النكرة مع عدم المغايرة كقوله تعالى :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A definite noun after an indefinite one can change scope: reconciliation for spouses becomes reconciliation generally, and punishment is added to prior punishment.
rows.anchor: فلا جناح عليهما أن يصلحا بينهما صلحا والصلح خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A definite noun may recur with a different referent, as when a later scripture confirms an earlier scripture.
rows.anchor: وقد تعاد المعرفة معرفة مع المغايرة كقوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish God’s complete power: the wonders of fig and olive creation, prophethood, and the human being—the cosmos’s most marvelous creature—support it.
rows.anchor: مقصودها سر مقصود { ألم نشرح } وذلك هو إثبات القدرة الكاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath signals the honor of these things and the sacred lands associated with prophets, whose histories and blessings display divine power.
rows.anchor: وأقسم فيها بأشياء أشار بها إلى شرفها في أنفسها وفي عجيب صنعها وشرف البقاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Linked to al-Sharḥ, the surah presents humanity and especially the Prophet as the finest created kind, Abraham as its noblest root, and Mecca as its best land; God raises or lowers whom He wills.
rows.anchor: خصه بأن جعل نوعه صلى الله عليه وسلم أكمل الأنواع وهو الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish God’s complete power: the wonders of fig and olive creation, prophethood, and the human being—the cosmos’s most marvelous creature—support it.
rows.anchor: مقصودها سر مقصود { ألم نشرح } وذلك هو إثبات القدرة الكاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its oaths point to the honor and marvels of the objects sworn by and of lands blessed by prophets and righteous people.
rows.anchor: وأقسم فيها بأشياء أشار بها إلى شرفها في أنفسها وفي عجيب صنعها وشرف البقاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah continues al-Sharḥ by presenting the Prophet’s kind as creation’s finest, Abraham as its noblest root, Mecca as the best land, and God as the one who raises or lowers whom He wills.
rows.anchor: خصه بأن جعل نوعه صلى الله عليه وسلم أكمل الأنواع وهو الإنسان
